films.title: GOODNIGHT IRENE
films.description: DAIS Skate Co.'s 25-minute debut full-length follows a tightly connected Northeast crew through New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, Rhode Island and Boston. Eleven end-title skaters, three additional credited appearances and Jimmy Politi's full-part credit make up the 15-person documented roster, filmed by Gorsky, Mike Geary and Shane "Sassy" Affuso with six additional camera contributors.
creditNotes: DAIS Skate Co.'s official upload identifies GOODNIGHT IRENE as its first official full-length and supplies the five-state filming geography.

The exact film's end titles were visually reviewed in the controlled official player. They credit Gorsky, Mike Geary and Shane 'Sassy' Affuso as main filmers; Isaac Doty, Jordan Green, Scott Williams, Joe Zarecki, Noah Yandive and Arron Sherry as additional filmers; 11 skaters; three separately billed additional appearances; and Jimmy Politi with a full part.
The roster is deliberately labeled first-party-only because no independent source with an equally complete credit roll was located. No unsupported formal director or editor credit is asserted.
films.locationNote: The official DAIS description explicitly states that the film was shot throughout New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, Rhode Island and Boston; no unsupported spot-by-spot itinerary is asserted.
films.historicalContext: GOODNIGHT IRENE is DAIS Skate Co.'s first official full-length, documenting the young brand's Northeast network across five states in 2026.
films.artworkNotes: The exact official upload's 1920x1080 YouTube max-resolution artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-16. It pairs a street-skating still with a large red film-specific title treatment and contains no trailer or episode labeling.

films.title: BANDOLIER
films.description: S.A.D. Skate All Day's 37-minute fourth full-length gives eight riders named chapters and folds six more into its Homies section. Rudy De La Torre and Cain Gallegos filmed the Southern California team video, which moves from Kristion Jordan and Daniel Weaver through Johnny Mercado, Carlos Torres, Kevin Hibbert, Joshua Willard, Jonathan Henderson and Presscott Frost.

The exact film's end titles were visually reviewed in the controlled official player. They credit Rudy De La Torre and Cain Gallegos with filming, Sketchfool with animation, 14 named skaters and 14 additional filming contributors.

The complete roster is deliberately labeled first-party-only because no independent source with an equally complete credit roll was located. No unsupported formal director or editor credit is asserted.

films.title: SAN FRANCISCO BURNING
films.description: Thrasher and Spitfire's 35-minute San Francisco full-length gathers 50 documented skaters entirely within city limits. Nick Michel, Jeff Carlyle, Diego Todd, Rob Bootes and Miles Silvas anchor Otto Ray's edit, while three dense montages and shared sections connect generations of locals and visitors across the city's best-known terrain.
creditNotes: Thrasher Magazine's official upload identifies Nick Michel, Jeff Carlyle, Diego Todd, Rob Bootes and Miles Silvas as principal names and states that the full-length was filmed entirely within San Francisco city limits.
Spitfire's first-party project page credits Otto Ray as editor and principal filmer, Cody Thompson, Brendan Bill and Tanner Rowe with filming, and Tom Shattuck with photography.

SkateVideoSite independently classifies the 35-minute release, preserves the section structure and indexes all 50 skaters plus 15 additional production contributors. It uses Rob Bootes while another contemporary listing uses Robby Bootes; the official upload spelling is retained. No unsupported formal director credit is asserted.
films.locationNote: Thrasher and Spitfire state that the film was shot entirely inside San Francisco city limits. Independent filmography notes identify 3rd & Army, China Banks, Bay Blocks, Pier 7, 3 Up 3 Down and Kezar Stadium among the documented spots.
films.historicalContext: Filmed for one year entirely within San Francisco, SAN FRANCISCO BURNING is Thrasher and Spitfire's 2026 city portrait, connecting major contemporary pros with deep local and visiting casts across three generations.
films.artworkNotes: The exact official upload's YouTube max-resolution artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-16. It combines dedicated flame-lettered SAN FRANCISCO BURNING and Thrasher branding with a fisheye rail-skating still and contains no trailer or episode labeling.
